text: “You don’t necessarily run into this on short cases. Today’s a long one, so it’s best to think ahead for your own clothes.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Then... why? Does everyone dress like that?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “At least here, we try not to wear our own undergarments during long operations. It's a nuisance if they get wet.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Wet? You mean from sweat?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That too. Irrigation fluid, blood... If you're unlucky, even your scrubs won't keep it all out.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Wait, even our own underwear can get blood on it?! Don’t make it sound like an everyday occurrence!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The younger nurse instinctively glanced down at her clothes. Watching her suddenly stiffen, Asakura's lips curled slightly upward.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe, what's so strange? We're performing surgery, not playing house.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “I know it's surgery! But I thought... well...”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You thought all the blood would stay obediently inside the patient and disappear once we were done?”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “You’re definitely picking out all the scariest parts to tell me!”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But I'm telling the truth.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura blinked, her smile so sweet it left little room for complaint.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If those cute pink panties of yours get a female patient's blood on them, won't that be awkward when you get home?”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “H-how did you even see the color?!”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I happened to catch a glimpse when you took off your ward uniform just now. I'm only worrying about them.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “You just want to see me embarrass myself, don’t you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I'm not. Think about it. Hospital clothes are easy to get washed. Ruining underwear you like isn't worth it.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Fine, I’ll change! I’m not sacrificing my favorite underwear.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Don't worry. Most of the time, proper protection keeps everything fine. It's just best to consider what might happen during a long operation before going in.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Why didn't you say the reassuring part first...?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Your expression was so amusing that I got a little carried away.”

speaker: Narrator
text: The younger nurse put her undergarments in the locker and dressed properly in her scrub trousers and top. She took a few steps, stopped, and discreetly tugged at the fabric of her trousers.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “What is it? Found something else this time?”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “The trousers... They rub a little when I walk, directly against my skin.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Mm.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “The top too. Without a bra, the fabric against my chest feels so rough...”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “I’m not imagining this, am I? Don’t you think this fabric is really rough?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “The first time I wore this fabric, I thought it was stiff too.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Huh? You did too?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course. I'm not made out of scrub fabric.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “I thought once you got used to it, you wouldn't even notice those things anymore.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You forget when you're busy. Especially when the doctor suddenly holds out a hand for an instrument. Who has time to think about their trousers chafing then?”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “That sounds a little frightening again...”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But this batch really is a bit stiff. Let me see.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura pinched her own sleeve and compared its fabric with the younger nurse's top, then checked inside the collar.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Mm, these must be from the new delivery. Older ones that have been washed are actually softer.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “So it's not just me being strange?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course not. Uncomfortable clothes are uncomfortable. Putting up with them won't make them softer.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “There are some spare sets that have softened in the wash in the next locker. I'll get you one. It should be your size.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Am I allowed to change?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Why wouldn't you, if you can? You'll be standing for hours today. You're not here for an endurance contest.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura took a folded set of scrubs from the spare locker and handed it over, then folded the stiff new set and put it aside to be checked.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I'll mention it to the director later. At least we can get more comfortable fabric next time.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “You even know which batch of clothes has problems?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If we have to wear something uncomfortable all day, of course I do. Patients aren't the only people we need to look after.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “...And you were being so mean just a moment ago.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm? What happened a moment ago?”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Are you really going to pretend you don't know?!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The younger nurse finally laughed. They each picked up a surgical cap and put it on. Asakura straightened the collar of the spare scrub top for her, then checked the cap's rim, which was not quite tucked into place

speaker: Narrator
text: yet.

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “You’re always saying you count as a newcomer at Hoshimi. You certainly don’t sound like one.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That's right.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “But you even know which batch of scrubs has bad fabric. And when you mentioned long operations, you sounded like you'd done lots of them.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I said I was inexperienced at Hoshimi, not that I learned to be a nurse today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “And tuck that side of your cap in properly. Keep your ears and the ends of your hair inside.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Yes! I will!”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura put on her mask and opened the door to the surgical corridor. The younger nurse hurried after her. Her face was still nervous, but her steps were much steadier than when she had entered the changing room.

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “If I really do get nervous at the table, you’ll give me a reminder, won’t you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “First, watch what I'm doing. Ask if you don't understand. Say so if you're unsure. That's much more useful than pretending to be calm.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “Understood.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Good. Then let's go see whether we really are playing house today.”

speaker: Shiori Yoneda
text: “You’re doing that on purpose!”

speaker: Narrator
text: Their voices gradually faded down the surgical corridor.

speaker: Narrator
text: The plaza is much busier on Sunday than on weekdays. Sakaguchi turns his phone over on the bench and looks up once more at the people passing by.

speaker: Narrator
text: He and Miyuki Asakura agreed to meet at two in the afternoon. Now the minute hand on the plaza clock has leisurely completed another lap.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…I hope nothing’s happened to her.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Sakaguchi calls again. The phone rings for a long time before someone finally answers.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Hello?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Asakura? Where are you now?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Mm… Dr. Sakaguchi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes, it’s me. Are you all right?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Rustling comes through the phone, followed by the dull thud of something falling onto the floor.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Aaah—!!!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What happened?!”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh no!! I overslept!!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Overslept?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Is today Sunday?! Were we supposed to meet at two?!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes. It’s ten past three now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Th-three?!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The other end falls silent for two seconds, then hurried footsteps follow.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Are you still waiting for me?!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I am.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m sorry! I’m so sorry! I’ll be right there!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Don’t rush. Were you on duty last night?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “No.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then how did you sleep until now?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s that drama I watched yesterday! The last episode ended on such an outrageous cliffhanger. How could I possibly stop there!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…So you watched all night?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Until sunrise. Then I thought I’d sleep for a little while… The next thing I knew, your call woke me.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Quite a ‘little while.’”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Don’t laugh! I’ll be there in twenty… no, thirty minutes!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Take your time. Just make sure you put your shoes on properly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi!!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The call ends. Sakaguchi looks at the dark screen, then up at the three-o’clock afternoon sky.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Asakura notices even a handover five minutes early at the hospital, and yet…”

speaker: Narrator
text: Forty minutes later, Asakura jogs over from the far side of the plaza. She is in light casual clothes with a small bag over her shoulder, her hair still showing the curves of a hurried styling.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi—!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You finally made it.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m sorry…”

speaker: Narrator
text: She presses her palms together, smiling sweetly and obediently. Before Sakaguchi can speak, Asakura raises her phone.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I promise, I really did set an alarm.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “For what time?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Eleven.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then why did you only wake up at three?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’d like to know too. My phone says I turned it off, but I don’t remember doing it at all.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You remember the hospital rota so clearly, but not turning off your own alarm?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That’s different. Patients are waiting at the hospital. Of course I can’t be careless.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “On a day off… nobody needs surgery just because I stay in bed a little longer.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Someone waited for you for over an hour today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Ooh… I admit that was my fault. What would it take for you to forgive me, Dr. Sakaguchi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Let’s at least get something to eat first. I’m getting hungry.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “All right! My treat today. You can have anything you like!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Really?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Well… except the kind of fancy restaurant you have to book three months ahead.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Quite a few conditions attached.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I haven’t even had breakfast yet. Have mercy on me first.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She gently tugs Sakaguchi’s sleeve and heads toward the shopping street. Her embarrassment doesn’t last long; there is already a spring in her step again.

speaker: Narrator
text: They enter a small restaurant still serving afternoon tea. Their window seat overlooks the pedestrians outside, and patterned paper menus lie on the table.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Huh… They’ve stopped serving the lunch set.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “It’s almost four.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I know. But I haven’t had lunch today.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So your lunchtime is nothing like the hospital’s.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s a rare day off. The clock ought to work around me.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I’ve never heard you say that at the hospital.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “How could I? If a patient is due at seven, it means seven. If an instrument is missing, can I say I’ll look for it after I’ve had my sleep?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So the moment you finish work, you become a completely different person?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Not a different person. This person finally gets to be lazy.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura orders a hot sandwich, then studies the dessert section intently.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you say you needed a meal? Why are you still looking at cake?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “The meal is for now. The cake is for afterward. Surely a doctor understands the order?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I thought you might have some special diet plan.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I do. Step one: feed the me who’s been hungry for half a day.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “And step two?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Make sure the handsome doctor who waited an hour for me enjoys his meal too.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Are you trying to sweet-talk me?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Can’t I? I’m very good at reassuring patients.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So I’m a patient today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you’d like, I could take care of you until you feel better.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Something about that doesn’t sound quite right.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. Let’s eat first, then. No more hospital talk.”

speaker: Narrator
text: The hot sandwich arrives. Asakura closes her eyes in satisfaction at the first bite, all her clever remarks momentarily defeated by food.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Good?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Mm! Try some. This sauce is delicious.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You were late, but now you sound like you’re showing me your favorite places.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course. Being late means I have to make the rest of our time even more worthwhile.”

speaker: Narrator
text: After they eat, sunlight slants across the table. Asakura taps her dessert glass with a small spoon and finally stops rushing to speak.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “When I watch you work, you really don’t seem like a newcomer.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “This again? Didn’t I tell you last time that I’m only new to Hoshimi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I mean, you seem to know all about handovers, operating-room routines, and exactly where newcomers will make mistakes.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Well… I’ve done all those things before.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Just how much were you responsible for?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Routine nursing, scheduling, training new staff… Later I was even the leader of the second nursing team.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Team leader?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Officially. I led a whole team on shift, and before leaving I had to make sure everyone had handed everything over properly.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then why have you kept calling yourself an inexperienced new nurse since coming to Hoshimi?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Because I really am unfamiliar with the people and systems here. The way my old hospital scheduled things doesn’t mean Hoshimi does the same.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That sounds quite conscientious.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you think that means I’m going to become meek and obedient, you’re wrong.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I wouldn’t dare think that now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “When I was promoted, everyone said it was a good thing. I could manage more people, and my words carried more weight.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “At first, I was happy too. Who doesn’t like having their work recognized?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “And then?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Then I found that everyone wanted me on their side.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “What should have been arranging nursing care for patients turned into guessing which superior might be upset first.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You didn’t like that kind of work?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I don’t mind managing things. Who should help when someone is overwhelmed; how to teach a newcomer until she understands—I like all that.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But smiling to appease people, finding out who’s fighting with whom, cleaning up messes for the higher-ups that have nothing to do with nursing… No, thank you.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Did you say that outright back then too?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Yes. Though whenever I did, someone would say I was immature.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You don’t look as though that would bother you now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It does. But one day I suddenly thought: why should those people get to decide whether I’m happy every day?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura scoops up a small spoonful of dessert, as though discussing something she has already thought through thoroughly.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I want to care for patients and teach newcomers. Those things interest me, so I’ll keep doing them.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I don’t want to take sides all day, or have dinner with people I dislike every evening after work. So I won’t be that kind of team leader anymore.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So coming to Hoshimi was your own choice?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course. You didn’t think I came here for retraining because I couldn’t do anything right at my old hospital, did you?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I never said that.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Good. Otherwise I might have to check your handover sheet again tomorrow.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Hey, weren’t we avoiding work talk today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, right. I nearly brought the hospital into our date again.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “But you really do seem happy now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I am. I can work hard, sleep in, watch dramas, and dress up to go out for good food.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m only twenty-three. Surely there’s more to look forward to than shifts and rotas?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Fair enough. What else would you like to do?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “So much. Go to the seaside, see a new film, sleep until I wake up naturally…”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You already managed the last one today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “And find a man I like the look of to take me on a date now and then.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm? Such a mild reaction?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said it so naturally.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It is perfectly natural.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Rather than flatter those awful, powerful doctors, I’d much rather tease a handsome doctor I actually like.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…You wouldn’t happen to mean me, would you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. What do you think?”

speaker: Narrator
text: She doesn’t rush to say anything else, merely sets her spoon back on the saucer and smiles at Sakaguchi.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You’re being deliberately vague.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It took me so long to get a whole day with you. Of course I have to make it interesting.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you only remember this date at three?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…You’re awful. Can we retire that joke now?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Who just said she wanted to make today interesting?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm… So Dr. Sakaguchi can talk back after all.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura smiles and reaches for the bill. Before Sakaguchi can say anything more, she is already on her way to the till.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Come on. The afternoon isn’t over yet.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Leaving the restaurant, they follow the shopping street to the river. A breeze blows along the waterside path, where the Sunday crowds are much thinner than in the shops.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said you like teaching newcomers. But sometimes you’re quite strict with them.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Am I? I thought I’d been exceptionally gentle here at Hoshimi.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Sometimes you even seem a little pleased to see someone nervous.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You caught me?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You admitted that far too quickly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Being nervous isn’t always bad. Newcomers ask me serious questions because they know how much they don’t understand.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Patients too. Some are scared, but still desperately want to hear what will happen next.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Do you mean that policewoman from before?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. She’s not the only one.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said we wouldn’t talk about the hospital today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “This is a personal interest, not a discussion about the rota. Two different things.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That sounds a little dangerous.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Shall I tell you something even more dangerous?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Let’s hear it.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura turns to face Sakaguchi and takes two steps backward. As if about to offer a serious professional opinion, she suddenly lowers her voice.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’ve always thought surgery is actually like an enormous SM play session.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Think about it. Outside, people can walk, sit, and make their own decisions. Once they enter the operating room, so much has to be left to the doctors and nurses.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…That’s true.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Where they lie, where their hands and feet go, when they can move… It’s their own body, but we set the pace for everything that follows.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That’s for the operation.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I know. But don’t you think that mixture of fear, embarrassment, and having to trust someone else… is rather intriguing?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I’ve never heard a nurse describe her work that way before.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. That just means the others hide it better.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You don’t actually treat patients as playthings, do you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course I do my job properly at work. I wouldn’t deliberately disrupt an operation just because I found something amusing.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But observing a patient’s reactions is part of a nurse’s skill. Terrified, yet unable to stop asking what comes next—sometimes they’re very easy to read.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So you just smile and wait for them to keep asking?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If they want to know, I can hardly rush to force the answers on them.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…No wonder you were so pleased that day.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Still, not every patient feels that way.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “In all the operations I’ve assisted with, quite a few young women have been both frightened and curious, always wondering what we’ll do next.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It doesn’t seem quite as obvious with older patients.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…You really do pay close attention.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I am a nurse, after all. Working out what a patient is actually worried about is part of the job.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She smiles and turns forward again, casually brushing the windblown hair away from her cheek.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Come to think of it… for some reason, almost all the patients at our hospital are young women.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi, don’t you think that’s a little strange?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I wouldn’t know how to answer that even if you asked me.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehehe. Very strange.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura walks on as though nothing happened, leaving Sakaguchi standing there wondering what exactly he has just been asked.

speaker: Narrator
text: The light gradually softens. They sit on a bench beside the river. Someone cycles past in the distance, and the bell soon fades into the breeze.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I can understand now why you don’t want to deal with factions and positions anymore.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “So serious all of a sudden?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You’re clearly better at managing people than many others. But from what you’ve said, you seem to know exactly what you don’t want.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It took me some time to work that out.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You and Serika used to work at the same hospital, didn’t you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Yes.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You came to Hoshimi together. Did something happen?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura gazes at the river, slowly gathering up the strap of the small bag beside her. She doesn’t answer right away.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Let’s leave what happened there, there.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Sorry. I shouldn’t have asked so suddenly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You don’t need to apologize. I know you’re curious.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “There are just some things I don’t want to talk about yet.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She turns back, still smiling, but this time she isn’t teasing him.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you want to get to know me… could you start with who I am now?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Of course.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That easily?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “If you don’t want to talk, I won’t ask.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Thank you.”

speaker: Narrator
text: The distant river reflects the sunset. Asakura looks away for a moment, then turns back to Sakaguchi as though something has occurred to her.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “There is one thing I’d like to ask you, though.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What is it?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “When you can, would you help Serika a little more?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Serika?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Sometimes she struggles to say what she wants to say. You’ve probably noticed that working with her.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…A little.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I can’t tell you those things for her. But if one day she wants to tell you herself… would you hear her out?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes. I’ll remember.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Then I’m counting on you.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She exhales softly, as though she has finally entrusted him with a small concern that has been on her mind.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “All right—! That’s enough serious talk for today!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You switch gears quickly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s a rare chance to go on a date. I don’t want the whole thing to feel like a nursing meeting.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What would you like to do next?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm… First, let’s see if that dessert shop is still open.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you just have cake?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That was afternoon tea. It’s almost dinnertime now.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Your sense of time really does follow its own rules.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “At the hospital, my time belongs to the patients and everyone else. I want to keep the rest of today for myself.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Fair enough.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “And you.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Huh?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Why else would I have rushed over today? Just to eat a sandwich on my own?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You make it sound as if you weren’t late.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, Sakaguchi-kun. Could we stop bringing that up for the rest of today?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Her “Sakaguchi-kun” comes lightly and naturally. As Sakaguchi turns, Asakura is already standing, holding out her hand.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…All right. I’ll let you off today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. You really are a good doctor.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What does being a doctor have to do with it?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You waited for me, listened to me, and will even join me for a second round of dessert. Very high marks.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You have some strange criteria.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You only just noticed?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Sakaguchi takes her outstretched hand, and they walk along the path toward the shopping street as the streetlights come on.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, and I’ll definitely be on time for our next date.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What time will you set your alarm?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Why don’t you call to wake me up?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Wouldn’t that be just like today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s different. Today I didn’t hear your good morning until three.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Next time… I’d like to hear it earlier.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She smiles, but doesn’t let go of his hand. Warm lights come on in the shop windows ahead.

speaker: Narrator
text: The plaza is much busier on Sunday than on weekdays. Sakaguchi turns his phone over on the bench and looks up once more at the people passing by.

speaker: Narrator
text: He and Miyuki Asakura agreed to meet at two in the afternoon. Now the minute hand on the plaza clock has leisurely completed another lap.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…I hope nothing’s happened to her.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Sakaguchi calls again. The phone rings for a long time before someone finally answers.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Hello?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Asakura? Where are you now?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Mm… Dr. Sakaguchi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes, it’s me. Are you all right?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Rustling comes through the phone, followed by the dull thud of something falling onto the floor.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Aaah—!!!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What happened?!”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh no!! I overslept!!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Overslept?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Is today Sunday?! Were we supposed to meet at two?!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes. It’s ten past three now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Th-three?!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The other end falls silent for two seconds, then hurried footsteps follow.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Are you still waiting for me?!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I am.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m sorry! I’m so sorry! I’ll be right there!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Don’t rush. Were you on duty last night?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “No.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then how did you sleep until now?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s that drama I watched yesterday! The last episode ended on such an outrageous cliffhanger. How could I possibly stop there!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…So you watched all night?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Until sunrise. Then I thought I’d sleep for a little while… The next thing I knew, your call woke me.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Quite a ‘little while.’”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Don’t laugh! I’ll be there in twenty… no, thirty minutes!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Take your time. Just make sure you put your shoes on properly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi!!”

speaker: Narrator
text: The call ends. Sakaguchi looks at the dark screen, then up at the three-o’clock afternoon sky.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Asakura notices even a handover five minutes early at the hospital, and yet…”

speaker: Narrator
text: Forty minutes later, Asakura jogs over from the far side of the plaza. She is in light casual clothes with a small bag over her shoulder, her hair still showing the curves of a hurried styling.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi—!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You finally made it.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m sorry…”

speaker: Narrator
text: She presses her palms together, smiling sweetly and obediently. Before Sakaguchi can speak, Asakura raises her phone.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I promise, I really did set an alarm.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “For what time?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Eleven.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then why did you only wake up at three?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’d like to know too. My phone says I turned it off, but I don’t remember doing it at all.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You remember the hospital rota so clearly, but not turning off your own alarm?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That’s different. Patients are waiting at the hospital. Of course I can’t be careless.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “On a day off… nobody needs surgery just because I stay in bed a little longer.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Someone waited for you for over an hour today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Ooh… I admit that was my fault. What would it take for you to forgive me, Dr. Sakaguchi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Let’s at least get something to eat first. I’m getting hungry.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “All right! My treat today. You can have anything you like!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Really?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Well… except the kind of fancy restaurant you have to book three months ahead.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Quite a few conditions attached.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I haven’t even had breakfast yet. Have mercy on me first.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She gently tugs Sakaguchi’s sleeve and heads toward the shopping street. Her embarrassment doesn’t last long; there is already a spring in her step again.

speaker: Narrator
text: They enter a small restaurant still serving afternoon tea. Their window seat overlooks the pedestrians outside, and patterned paper menus lie on the table.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Huh… They’ve stopped serving the lunch set.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “It’s almost four.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I know. But I haven’t had lunch today.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So your lunchtime is nothing like the hospital’s.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s a rare day off. The clock ought to work around me.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I’ve never heard you say that at the hospital.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “How could I? If a patient is due at seven, it means seven. If an instrument is missing, can I say I’ll look for it after I’ve had my sleep?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So the moment you finish work, you become a completely different person?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Not a different person. This person finally gets to be lazy.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura orders a hot sandwich, then studies the dessert section intently.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you say you needed a meal? Why are you still looking at cake?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “The meal is for now. The cake is for afterward. Surely a doctor understands the order?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I thought you might have some special diet plan.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I do. Step one: feed the me who’s been hungry for half a day.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “And step two?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Make sure the handsome doctor who waited an hour for me enjoys his meal too.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Are you trying to sweet-talk me?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Can’t I? I’m very good at reassuring patients.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So I’m a patient today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you’d like, I could take care of you until you feel better.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Something about that doesn’t sound quite right.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. Let’s eat first, then. No more hospital talk.”

speaker: Narrator
text: The hot sandwich arrives. Asakura closes her eyes in satisfaction at the first bite, all her clever remarks momentarily defeated by food.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Good?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Mm! Try some. This sauce is delicious.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You were late, but now you sound like you’re showing me your favorite places.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course. Being late means I have to make the rest of our time even more worthwhile.”

speaker: Narrator
text: After they eat, sunlight slants across the table. Asakura taps her dessert glass with a small spoon and finally stops rushing to speak.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “When I watch you work, you really don’t seem like a newcomer.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “This again? Didn’t I tell you last time that I’m only new to Hoshimi?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I mean, you seem to know all about handovers, operating-room routines, and exactly where newcomers will make mistakes.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Well… I’ve done all those things before.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Just how much were you responsible for?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Routine nursing, scheduling, training new staff… Later I was even the leader of the second nursing team.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Team leader?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Officially. I led a whole team on shift, and before leaving I had to make sure everyone had handed everything over properly.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Then why have you kept calling yourself an inexperienced new nurse since coming to Hoshimi?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Because I really am unfamiliar with the people and systems here. The way my old hospital scheduled things doesn’t mean Hoshimi does the same.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That sounds quite conscientious.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you think that means I’m going to become meek and obedient, you’re wrong.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I wouldn’t dare think that now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “When I was promoted, everyone said it was a good thing. I could manage more people, and my words carried more weight.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “At first, I was happy too. Who doesn’t like having their work recognized?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “And then?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Then I found that everyone wanted me on their side.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “What should have been arranging nursing care for patients turned into guessing which superior might be upset first.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You didn’t like that kind of work?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I don’t mind managing things. Who should help when someone is overwhelmed; how to teach a newcomer until she understands—I like all that.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But smiling to appease people, finding out who’s fighting with whom, cleaning up messes for the higher-ups that have nothing to do with nursing… No, thank you.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Did you say that outright back then too?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Yes. Though whenever I did, someone would say I was immature.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You don’t look as though that would bother you now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It does. But one day I suddenly thought: why should those people get to decide whether I’m happy every day?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura scoops up a small spoonful of dessert, as though discussing something she has already thought through thoroughly.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I want to care for patients and teach newcomers. Those things interest me, so I’ll keep doing them.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I don’t want to take sides all day, or have dinner with people I dislike every evening after work. So I won’t be that kind of team leader anymore.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So coming to Hoshimi was your own choice?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course. You didn’t think I came here for retraining because I couldn’t do anything right at my old hospital, did you?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I never said that.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Good. Otherwise I might have to check your handover sheet again tomorrow.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Hey, weren’t we avoiding work talk today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, right. I nearly brought the hospital into our date again.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “But you really do seem happy now.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I am. I can work hard, sleep in, watch dramas, and dress up to go out for good food.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’m only twenty-three. Surely there’s more to look forward to than shifts and rotas?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Fair enough. What else would you like to do?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “So much. Go to the seaside, see a new film, sleep until I wake up naturally…”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You already managed the last one today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “And find a man I like the look of to take me on a date now and then.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm? Such a mild reaction?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said it so naturally.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It is perfectly natural.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Rather than flatter those awful, powerful doctors, I’d much rather tease a handsome doctor I actually like.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…You wouldn’t happen to mean me, would you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. What do you think?”

speaker: Narrator
text: She doesn’t rush to say anything else, merely sets her spoon back on the saucer and smiles at Sakaguchi.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You’re being deliberately vague.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It took me so long to get a whole day with you. Of course I have to make it interesting.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you only remember this date at three?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…You’re awful. Can we retire that joke now?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Who just said she wanted to make today interesting?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm… So Dr. Sakaguchi can talk back after all.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura smiles and reaches for the bill. Before Sakaguchi can say anything more, she is already on her way to the till.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Come on. The afternoon isn’t over yet.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Leaving the restaurant, they follow the shopping street to the river. A breeze blows along the waterside path, where the Sunday crowds are much thinner than in the shops.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said you like teaching newcomers. But sometimes you’re quite strict with them.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Am I? I thought I’d been exceptionally gentle here at Hoshimi.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Sometimes you even seem a little pleased to see someone nervous.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You caught me?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You admitted that far too quickly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Being nervous isn’t always bad. Newcomers ask me serious questions because they know how much they don’t understand.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Patients too. Some are scared, but still desperately want to hear what will happen next.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Do you mean that policewoman from before?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. She’s not the only one.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You said we wouldn’t talk about the hospital today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “This is a personal interest, not a discussion about the rota. Two different things.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That sounds a little dangerous.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Shall I tell you something even more dangerous?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Let’s hear it.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura turns to face Sakaguchi and takes two steps backward. As if about to offer a serious professional opinion, she suddenly lowers her voice.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I’ve always thought surgery is actually like an enormous SM play session.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Think about it. Outside, people can walk, sit, and make their own decisions. Once they enter the operating room, so much has to be left to the doctors and nurses.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…That’s true.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Where they lie, where their hands and feet go, when they can move… It’s their own body, but we set the pace for everything that follows.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “That’s for the operation.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I know. But don’t you think that mixture of fear, embarrassment, and having to trust someone else… is rather intriguing?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I’ve never heard a nurse describe her work that way before.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. That just means the others hide it better.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You don’t actually treat patients as playthings, do you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Of course I do my job properly at work. I wouldn’t deliberately disrupt an operation just because I found something amusing.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “But observing a patient’s reactions is part of a nurse’s skill. Terrified, yet unable to stop asking what comes next—sometimes they’re very easy to read.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “So you just smile and wait for them to keep asking?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If they want to know, I can hardly rush to force the answers on them.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…No wonder you were so pleased that day.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Still, not every patient feels that way.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “In all the operations I’ve assisted with, quite a few young women have been both frightened and curious, always wondering what we’ll do next.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It doesn’t seem quite as obvious with older patients.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…You really do pay close attention.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I am a nurse, after all. Working out what a patient is actually worried about is part of the job.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She smiles and turns forward again, casually brushing the windblown hair away from her cheek.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Come to think of it… for some reason, almost all the patients at our hospital are young women.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi, don’t you think that’s a little strange?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I wouldn’t know how to answer that even if you asked me.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehehe. Very strange.”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura walks on as though nothing happened, leaving Sakaguchi standing there wondering what exactly he has just been asked.

speaker: Narrator
text: The light gradually softens. They sit on a bench beside the river. Someone cycles past in the distance, and the bell soon fades into the breeze.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “I can understand now why you don’t want to deal with factions and positions anymore.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “So serious all of a sudden?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You’re clearly better at managing people than many others. But from what you’ve said, you seem to know exactly what you don’t want.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It took me some time to work that out.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You and Serika used to work at the same hospital, didn’t you?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Yes.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You came to Hoshimi together. Did something happen?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Asakura gazes at the river, slowly gathering up the strap of the small bag beside her. She doesn’t answer right away.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Dr. Sakaguchi.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Let’s leave what happened there, there.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Sorry. I shouldn’t have asked so suddenly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You don’t need to apologize. I know you’re curious.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “There are just some things I don’t want to talk about yet.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She turns back, still smiling, but this time she isn’t teasing him.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “If you want to get to know me… could you start with who I am now?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Of course.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That easily?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “If you don’t want to talk, I won’t ask.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Thank you.”

speaker: Narrator
text: The distant river reflects the sunset. Asakura looks away for a moment, then turns back to Sakaguchi as though something has occurred to her.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “There is one thing I’d like to ask you, though.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What is it?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “When you can, would you help Serika a little more?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Serika?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Sometimes she struggles to say what she wants to say. You’ve probably noticed that working with her.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…A little.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “I can’t tell you those things for her. But if one day she wants to tell you herself… would you hear her out?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Yes. I’ll remember.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Then I’m counting on you.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She exhales softly, as though she has finally entrusted him with a small concern that has been on her mind.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “All right—! That’s enough serious talk for today!”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You switch gears quickly.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s a rare chance to go on a date. I don’t want the whole thing to feel like a nursing meeting.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What would you like to do next?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hmm… First, let’s see if that dessert shop is still open.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Didn’t you just have cake?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “That was afternoon tea. It’s almost dinnertime now.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Your sense of time really does follow its own rules.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “At the hospital, my time belongs to the patients and everyone else. I want to keep the rest of today for myself.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…Fair enough.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “And you.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Huh?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Why else would I have rushed over today? Just to eat a sandwich on my own?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You make it sound as if you weren’t late.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, Sakaguchi-kun. Could we stop bringing that up for the rest of today?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Her “Sakaguchi-kun” comes lightly and naturally. As Sakaguchi turns, Asakura is already standing, holding out her hand.

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “…All right. I’ll let you off today.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Hehe. You really are a good doctor.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What does being a doctor have to do with it?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You waited for me, listened to me, and will even join me for a second round of dessert. Very high marks.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “You have some strange criteria.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “You only just noticed?”

speaker: Narrator
text: Sakaguchi takes her outstretched hand, and they walk along the path toward the shopping street as the streetlights come on.

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Oh, and I’ll definitely be on time for our next date.”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “What time will you set your alarm?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “…Why don’t you call to wake me up?”

speaker: Takashi Sakaguchi
text: “Wouldn’t that be just like today?”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “It’s different. Today I didn’t hear your good morning until three.”

speaker: Miyuki Asakura
text: “Next time… I’d like to hear it earlier.”

speaker: Narrator
text: She smiles, but doesn’t let go of his hand. Warm lights come on in the shop windows ahead.
